User Story: As a user, I want a docked input bar in the corner of the app, so that I can start a chat from anywhere without opening the full chat surface.
Expected Behavior (from code): A fixed bottom-right bar shows an "Ask anything..." input; focusing it opens the chat pane (onOpen) and pressing Enter (without Shift) submits the trimmed message, clearing the field; the send button is disabled until text is entered.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot as a side pane I can resize and place left/middle/right, so that I can work alongside my notes.
Expected Behavior (from code): ChatSidebar renders a resizable pane (drag handle, 360-1600px, persisted to localStorage x:right-pane-width), supports placement middle/right and pane sizes (chat-smaller/equal/bigger), and clamps width so the main pane keeps a minimum.

User Story: As a user, I want to expand the chat to full width and dock it back, so that I can switch between focused chat and split view.
Expected Behavior (from code): A header arrow button toggles maximize via onOpenFullScreen; when maximized the pane grows into freed space (flex 1 1 auto) and the empty state renders in a wider centered column; icon/tooltip flip between "Expand chat" and "Dock to side pane" based on placement and state.

Feature: Chat header with title + recent dropdown
User Story: As a user, I want the active chat title with a dropdown of recent chats, so that I can see and switch what I'm working on.
Expected Behavior (from code): ChatHeader shows the active chat title with a message icon; clicking opens a dropdown listing up to 6 recent runs (title + relative time, active highlighted) with a "View all chats" entry; renders as static text when no history exists.

User Story: As a user, I want to start a fresh chat, so that I can begin an unrelated conversation.
Expected Behavior (from code): A "+" button (tooltip "New chat") in the header invokes onNewChatTab, which resets the active tab to a new run with cleared conversation/draft; the same action is offered from the empty state and history view.

User Story: As a new/returning user, I want a greeting with recent chats and starter prompts, so that I can resume or quickly start a task.
Expected Behavior (from code): ChatEmptyState shows "What are we working on?", up to 4 recent chats (selectable, with View all), and 3 starter action cards (Draft a reply, Set up a background agent, Research a topic) that fill the composer via onPickPrompt without submitting.

User Story: As a user, I want one-click suggestion chips, so that I can launch common tasks (draft email, meeting prep, document, organize files, presentation).
Expected Behavior (from code): The Suggestions component renders pill buttons each with an icon/label; clicking calls onSelect with the suggestion's prompt template (e.g. "Let's draft an email response to [name]"), supporting horizontal or vertical layout.

User Story: As a user, I want a full list of all chats with created times, so that I can browse and reopen past conversations.
Expected Behavior (from code): ChatHistoryView lists runs sorted newest-first with title and relative created time, a sticky column header, an empty "No chats yet" state, and Search/New chat actions; rows select a run (cmd-click opens in new tab).

User Story: As a user, I want to delete a chat after confirming, so that I can remove conversations I no longer need without accidental loss.
Expected Behavior (from code): Right-click a history row opens a context menu with a destructive Delete (hidden while the run is processing); choosing it opens a confirm dialog, and confirming calls onDeleteRun (runs:delete).

User Story: As a user, I want to open a chat in a separate tab, so that I can keep multiple conversations side by side.
Expected Behavior (from code): Cmd-clicking a history row, or selecting "Open in new tab" from its context menu, calls onOpenInNewTab(runId); chat tabs hold independent per-tab state (runId, conversation, draft, permissions).

User Story: As a user, I want to export the current chat's run log, so that I can debug or archive the conversation.
Expected Behavior (from code): The header "..." (Chat options) menu offers "Download chat log", enabled only when a run exists; it invokes runs:downloadLog which opens a Save dialog and copies runs/<runId>.jsonl to the chosen path, toasting success/failure.

User Story: As a user, I want the conversation to follow new messages but let me scroll up, so that I can read history without being yanked down.
Expected Behavior (from code): Conversation tracks bottom proximity; while at bottom it stays pinned, and when scrolled up a floating "Scroll to latest message" button appears; it also supports anchoring the viewport to a specific message id (used when sending).

User Story: As a user, I want messages rendered with markdown, so that bold, lists, links and code survive and assistant/user are visually distinct.
Expected Behavior (from code): User messages render right-aligned in a secondary bubble (with remarkBreaks preserving single newlines); assistant messages render full-width markdown via Streamdown; a "Thinking..." shimmer shows while processing before any text streams.

User Story: As a user, I want errors shown inline (but billing noise suppressed), so that I understand failures without confusing clutter.
Expected Behavior (from code): Error items render in a destructive-tinted banner with monospaced text; messages matching a known billing error are filtered out (return null) so they are handled elsewhere.

User Story: As a user, I want to type and send a message, so that I can talk to the copilot.
Expected Behavior (from code): PromptInputTextarea sends on Enter (Shift+Enter inserts a newline, IME composition respected); submit is blocked unless there is trimmed text or an attachment and the run is idle; sending clears text, mentions and attachments and creates a run if none exists.

User Story: As a user, I want to stop the assistant mid-response and force-kill if it hangs, so that I stay in control of long runs.
Expected Behavior (from code): While processing the send button becomes a Stop (square) button calling onStop (runs:stop); a second click enters force mode (spinner, destructive styling, tooltip "Click again to force stop") which passes force to terminate processes.

User Story: As a user, I want to attach files/images via picker, drag-drop, or paste, so that the copilot can use them.
Expected Behavior (from code): The "+" menu and drag-drop add files (<=10MB each, else toast error), reading them base64 to detect mime and show image thumbnails; staged attachments render as removable chips and are sent as attachment content parts.

User Story: As a user, I want my sent attachments shown in the transcript, so that I can see what I attached.
Expected Behavior (from code): ChatMessageAttachments renders images as previews (thumbnail/file URL with base64 fallback on error) and non-image files as labeled cards with type-specific icons, right-aligned under the user message.

User Story: As a user, I want to set a working directory for a chat (with recents), so that the agent operates in the right project folder.
Expected Behavior (from code): The "+" submenu lets the user choose/change/clear a work dir (defaulting to knowledge/Workspace), shows up to 3 recent dirs persisted in config/recent-work-dirs.json, displays a removable chip, and flushes the dir onto the run on first send.

User Story: As a user, I want to toggle web search for my message, so that the assistant can search the web when needed.
Expected Behavior (from code): A Globe toggle appears only when search is available (signed-in via gateway or an exa-search.json API key); when on it passes searchEnabled and stays on for the session until turned off; it expands to show a "Search" label.

User Story: As a user, I want to choose auto-approval vs manual approval prompts per chat, so that I can balance speed and safety.
Expected Behavior (from code): A ShieldCheck toggle switches between Auto and Manual before a run exists; once the run is created the mode is frozen to the run's permissionMode and the control becomes disabled with an explanatory tooltip.

User Story: As a user, I want to enable code mode and pick Claude Code or Codex, so that coding tasks are delegated to an on-device coding agent.
Expected Behavior (from code): When the code-mode feature flag is on, a Terminal chip toggles code mode and a second segment swaps the coding agent (Claude/Codex), persisted per work dir in config/coding-agents.json; the chosen agent is passed as codeMode on send and routes to the code_agent_run tool.

User Story: As a user, I want to pick the model for a new chat, so that I control which LLM answers.
Expected Behavior (from code): A dropdown lists configured models (gateway models when signed in, else providers from config/models.json) and sets the model only for the next run; once a run exists it is replaced by a read-only label fixed to the run's resolved provider/model.
Fix Applied: E05: Initialize the composer's selected model from the config active default so shown and used model agree.

User Story: As a user, I want to dictate a message, so that I can compose hands-free.
Expected Behavior (from code): A Mic button (shown when voice is available) starts a recording bar with an animated waveform and live/connecting status; Enter transcribes/submits, Escape/X cancels; transcription is auto-submitted as the message and flagged voiceInput.

User Story: As a user, I want the assistant to read responses aloud, so that I can listen instead of read.
Expected Behavior (from code): A Headphones toggle (shown when TTS available) enables voice output and a chevron menu picks "Speak summary" or "Speak full response"; the choice is sent as voiceOutput with each message and synthesized via voice:synthesize.

User Story: As a user, I want parsed voice commands shown for review before they run, so that destructive actions aren't taken without my consent.
Expected Behavior (from code): VoiceCommandConfirmation summarizes the parsed intent (email triage/reply/rule, meeting record start/stop, open command, insert text); email.triage requires explicit confirmation, and confirming invokes voice:executeCommand, closing on success.

User Story: As a user, I want my unsent text kept per chat and starter prompts to prefill, so that I don't lose work when switching tabs.
Expected Behavior (from code): The composer restores its tab draft on mount and reports changes via onDraftChange; a presetMessage (from empty-state cards or suggestions) sets the input then is consumed, and the textarea auto-focuses on the active tab.

User Story: As a user, I want to @-mention knowledge files, so that the assistant reads them as context.
Expected Behavior (from code): Typing "@" opens MentionPopover ranking files visible > recent > rest, filtered by query, navigable by arrows/Tab/Enter (Esc closes); selecting inserts "@displayName" and registers a FileMention sent as a markdown attachment content part.
Fix Applied: E04: Gate the popover key handler on filtered list length > 0 so Enter falls through to submit when empty.

User Story: As a user, I want mentions visually highlighted and deletable as a unit, so that they read clearly and edit cleanly.
Expected Behavior (from code): An overlay highlights "@label" segments behind the textarea (kept scroll-synced); Backspace right after a mention deletes the entire "@label" token and removes it from mention state, and Backspace on empty input removes the last attachment.

User Story: As a user editing a note, I want to drop an inline @solomon instruction, so that the copilot can act on a specific spot in the document.
Expected Behavior (from code): RowboatMentionPopover anchors a small textarea prefixed "@solomon"; Cmd/Ctrl/Shift+Enter (or Add) submits the instruction via onAdd, Escape/outside-click closes, and an optional Remove clears an existing instruction.

User Story: As a user, I want the note I'm viewing sent as context, so that the copilot answers about what's on screen.
Expected Behavior (from code): On each send the app builds middlePaneContext (e.g. the currently open note's path and content) and passes it to runs:createMessage so the agent has the active editor context.

User Story: As a user, I want each tool call shown as a collapsible card with inputs and outputs, so that I can inspect what the assistant did.
Expected Behavior (from code): Tool renders a collapsible card with a status lead icon (spinner/check/cross), a display title, and tabbed Parameters/Result content (errors shown in destructive styling, pending shown until output arrives).

User Story: As a user, I want consecutive tool calls collapsed into one "Ran N tools" group, so that the transcript stays readable.
Expected Behavior (from code): ToolGroupComponent collapses a run of tool calls into a single card showing a rolling/animated summary ("Ran N tools - actions"), derives group state from child statuses, and expands to per-tool collapsible rows.

User Story: As a user, I want live shell/command output to stream into the tool card, so that I can watch long-running commands.
Expected Behavior (from code): When a tool has streamingOutput the card shows an auto-scrolling terminal pre (TerminalOutput) instead of the tabbed view, sticking to the bottom unless the user scrolls up; fed by tool-output-stream events from executeCommand.

User Story: As a user, I want to see the model's reasoning with a duration, so that I understand how it thought without it cluttering the chat.
Expected Behavior (from code): Reasoning auto-opens while streaming (showing a "Thinking..." shimmer), records elapsed seconds, and auto-collapses ~1s after streaming ends ("Thought for N seconds"); the user can re-expand it.

User Story: As a user, I want web-search results shown as a rich card, so that I can see which sites were searched and open them.
Expected Behavior (from code): WebSearchResult animates a rolling reveal of fetched domains then settles on a favicon stack + "Searched X, Y and N others" summary; expanding shows the query and a clickable result list (opens in browser) with a source count.

User Story: As a user, I want memory-search results as clickable source rows, so that I can open the notes the answer came from.
Expected Behavior (from code): MemorySearchSources renders a "Memory - N sources" collapsible showing each hit's note title, relevance score, and a snippet with matched spans bolded; clicking a row opens the source knowledge note.

User Story: As a user, I want file paths the assistant mentions to render as clickable cards, so that I can open them directly.
Expected Behavior (from code): FilePathCard renders knowledge files (Open, opens in app), audio files (inline play/pause + Open), and other files (type icon, image thumbnail, Open via shell:openPath), driven by filepath code blocks.

User Story: As a user, I want app-navigation actions shown as status cards, so that I can see when the assistant opens notes/views or edits bases.
Expected Behavior (from code): AppActionCard shows the action label with an action-specific icon and a status indicator (spinner while running, green check when complete, "Failed" on error) for open-note/open-view/update-base-view/create-base.

User Story: As a user, I want a connect card when a third-party service is needed, so that I can OAuth-link it inline.
Expected Behavior (from code): legacy integration vendorConnectCard shows the toolkit, a Connect button that calls legacy-integration-vendor:initiate-connection, reflects connecting/connected/error states from legacy-integration-vendor:didConnect events, offers Retry on failure, and fires onConnected once.

User Story: As a user, I want to approve or deny tool actions, so that I control what the assistant executes on my machine.
Expected Behavior (from code): PermissionRequest shows the requested tool with command/file paths/arguments and Approve/Deny buttons; responding collapses to a header (re-expandable) showing Granted/Denied, and calls onPermissionResponse via runs:authorizePermission.

User Story: As a user, I want to approve a command just once, for the session, or always, so that I avoid repeated prompts for trusted actions.
Expected Behavior (from code): For command/file permissions, the Approve button has a dropdown offering "Allow for Session" and "Always Allow", calling onApproveSession/onApproveAlways so the scope is recorded for future requests.

User Story: As a user, I want to swap Claude Code/Codex when a coding command is requested, so that I can retry with the other agent in one click.
Expected Behavior (from code): When the requested command is an acpx coding-agent invocation, the card shows the agent badge and a "Use [other] instead" button that calls onSwitchAgent to retry with the alternate coding agent.

User Story: As a user, I want auto-approved/denied actions explained, so that I understand what auto mode allowed or blocked and why.
Expected Behavior (from code): AutoPermissionDecision renders an "Auto Allowed"/"Auto Denied" card with the tool name, reason, and command/file paths; in the transcript an "Auto-approved" hover hint with the reason is appended to auto-allowed tool cards.

User Story: As a user, I want the assistant to pause and ask me a question (free text or options), so that I can steer it when it's unsure.
Expected Behavior (from code): AskHumanRequest shows the agent's question; if options are provided it renders option buttons, otherwise an auto-focused textarea (Enter sends), and the answer is returned via onAskHumanResponse through runs:provideHumanInput.
Fix Applied: E01: Pass options={request.options} to AskHumanRequest in chat-sidebar.tsx.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to pull in specialized playbooks, so that it follows the right workflow for my task.
Expected Behavior (from code): The loadSkill tool resolves a skill id/path and returns its guidance; instructions list a catalog (draft-emails, meeting-prep, doc-collab, code-with-agents, background-task, live-note, browser-control, app-navigation, legacy-integration-vendor/mcp-integration, etc.) the agent must load before acting.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to read/write/edit/organize files anywhere on my machine, so that it can do real work on my documents and knowledge base.
Expected Behavior (from code): Builtin file tools cover getRoot/exists/stat/list/readText/writeText/editText/remove(trash)/glob/grep/mkdir/rename/copy with relative-to-workspace path resolution; out-of-workspace ops flow through the permission system.

User Story: As a user, I want conceptual recall over my notes, so that the copilot finds relevant context even without exact keywords.
Expected Behavior (from code): The memory-search tool runs semantic + lexical search over the knowledge vault (RFC 021), returning ranked chunks with file backlinks and falling back to lexical search; results render as the memory sources card.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to read PDFs, Office docs, and images, so that it can use non-text files as context.
Expected Behavior (from code): parseFile extracts text locally from PDF/XLSX/CSV/DOCX; LLMParse sends documents/images to the configured LLM as a multimodal attachment to produce markdown for scanned/complex files, capturing usage analytics.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to run shell commands, so that it can perform tasks beyond file edits.
Expected Behavior (from code): executeCommand runs a shell command in the workspace (or given cwd), streams stdout/stderr live, registers the process for force-kill, and returns exit code; non-preapproved commands trigger a one-time approval prompt.

User Story: As a user, I want coding tasks delegated to Claude Code/Codex, so that complex software work is handled by a dedicated coding agent.
Expected Behavior (from code): code_agent_run runs the selected on-device coding agent (chip is source of truth) in a project folder, streams tool calls/diffs/plan as code-run-events, surfaces inline permission requests, and reuses one persistent session per chat.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to search the web, so that it can answer with current information.
Expected Behavior (from code): The web-search tool queries Exa (via signed-in proxy or local exa-search.json key), supports a category and result count, and returns titles/urls/highlights/full text; availability gates the composer Globe toggle.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to remember preferences and context about me, so that it improves over time without me repeating myself.
Expected Behavior (from code): The save-to-memory tool appends a timestamped observation to knowledge/Agent Notes/inbox.md; instructions tell the agent to call it proactively for preferences, relationships, and explicit instructions, capturing situational context.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to drive the app UI, so that it can open notes, switch views, and filter/search bases for me.
Expected Behavior (from code): The app-navigation tool performs open-note, open-view (bases/graph), update-base-view (filters/columns/sort/search), get-base-state (scan frontmatter properties), and create-base; results render as app action cards.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to operate the embedded browser, so that it can open sites and interact with live pages.
Expected Behavior (from code): The browser-control tool reads the current page, inspects indexed interactable elements, and navigates/clicks/types/presses keys; load-browser-skill fetches site-specific recipes/selectors (load/list/refresh) surfaced as suggestedSkills.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to discover and run MCP tools, so that it can use external integrations I've configured.
Expected Behavior (from code): Builtin tools addMcpServer (validated), listMcpServers, listMcpTools, and executeMcpTool let the agent register and run MCP tools; instructions forbid hand-editing config/mcp.json.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to use Gmail/Slack/GitHub/Notion etc., so that it can act across my connected services.
Expected Behavior (from code): legacy-integration-vendor-list-toolkits / -search-tools / -execute-tool / -connect-toolkit discover, run, and OAuth-connect curated toolkits; all gated by islegacy integration vendorConfigured, and execute checks the account is ACTIVE before acting.

User Story: As a user, I want to set up recurring self-running tasks from chat, so that the copilot maintains digests or performs scheduled actions.
Expected Behavior (from code): create-background-task materializes bg-tasks/<slug> (task.yaml/index.md/runs) with optional cron/window/event triggers; patch-background-task edits one (extend-don't-fork); run-background-task-agent runs it now with optional one-off context.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to refresh or backfill a live note on demand, so that a self-updating note reflects new info now.
Expected Behavior (from code): run-live-note-agent manually runs the live-note agent on a note that has a live: frontmatter block, accepting optional one-off context (e.g. backfill from synced emails) and returning the action, summary, and new body.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to send native notifications with clickable deep links, so that it can alert me and land me on the right note/view.
Expected Behavior (from code): The notify-user tool shows an OS notification (title/message/optional action buttons) whose link opens an http(s):// URL in the browser or a solomon-ai:// deep link inside the app; gated by notification support.

User Story: As a user, I want the copilot to inspect an agent definition, so that it can reason about that agent's tools and structure.
Expected Behavior (from code): analyzeAgent fetches an agent file by name and returns its name, description, model, tool list/count, and whether it nests sub-agents.

User Story: As a user, I want one capable copilot whose abilities adapt to my setup, so that it knows my tools, OS, and connected services.
Expected Behavior (from code): buildCopilotAgent assembles the "solomon-ai" agent from all BuiltinTools; instructions are built dynamically with runtime OS/shell context, the skill catalog, and legacy integration vendor sections, excluding skills/sections (legacy-integration-vendor, code-with-agents) when those features are off.

User Story: As a user, I want a condensed transcript for non-chat surfaces, so that I can review a run's messages and tool calls in panels.
Expected Behavior (from code): CompactConversation renders the same conversation items in a compact form (right-aligned user bubbles, full-width assistant markdown, collapsible tool rows, error banners) for the live-note "Last run" tab and background-task run drill-downs.

Feature: legacy integration vendor connection refresh on connect
User Story: As a user, I want the chat to react when I connect a service mid-conversation, so that the assistant can immediately use it.
Expected Behavior (from code): ChatSidebar forwards onlegacy integration vendorConnected from connect cards; the input also subscribes to oauth:didConnect to refresh sign-in state, and connecting updates available models/search/tools without a restart.

User Story: As a note-taker, I want to bold selected text from the toolbar, so that I can emphasize key words.
Expected Behavior (from code): Clicking the Bold button runs editor.chain().focus().toggleBold() and shows an active state when the cursor is in bold text (Ctrl/Cmd+B).

User Story: As a note-taker, I want to italicize text, so that I can stress phrases.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Italic button toggles the italic mark via toggleItalic() and reflects active state (Ctrl/Cmd+I).

User Story: As a writer, I want to format inline code, so that code spans render monospaced.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Inline Code button toggles the code mark via toggleCode().

User Story: As a writer, I want to apply heading levels 1-3, so that I can structure my note.
Expected Behavior (from code): Three heading buttons call toggleHeading({level}) for levels 1/2/3; StarterKit is configured to allow only those levels.

User Story: As a writer, I want unordered lists, so that I can jot points.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Bullet List button toggles bulletList via toggleBulletList().

User Story: As a writer, I want numbered lists, so that I can sequence steps.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Ordered List button toggles orderedList via toggleOrderedList(); serialized as "1. " prefixes.

User Story: As a planner, I want checkable to-do items, so that I can track tasks inline.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Task List button toggles a nested TaskList/TaskItem; items serialize to "- [ ]"/"- [x]" markdown.

User Story: As a writer, I want blockquotes, so that I can quote sources.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Blockquote button toggles blockquote via toggleBlockquote(); serialized with "> " prefixes.

User Story: As a developer, I want fenced code blocks with a language, so that code is preserved verbatim.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Code Block button toggles codeBlock; serialized as ``` fences and the cursor line offset accounts for the fence.

User Story: As a writer, I want a divider, so that I can separate sections.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Horizontal Rule button inserts a rule via setHorizontalRule(); serialized as "---".

User Story: As a writer, I want to add, edit, open, or remove a hyperlink, so that I can reference URLs.
Expected Behavior (from code): A popover takes a URL (auto-prefixes https:// unless mailto), applies it over the selection via setLink, and when a link is active offers Open-in-browser and Remove; Enter applies, Escape cancels.

User Story: As a writer, I want to insert images, so that notes can hold visuals.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Image button opens a file picker (accept image/*) and routes the file through createImageUploadHandler, which inserts a placeholder then the saved image; the toolbar only shows when onImageUpload is provided.

User Story: As a user, I want to export a note to Markdown, PDF, or Word, so that I can share it.
Expected Behavior (from code): The Export dropdown calls onExport(format); App invokes export:note which opens a Save dialog with format-specific filters and writes the converted file.

User Story: As a note-taker, I want [[ ]] autocomplete that can create new notes, so that I can link my vault quickly.
Expected Behavior (from code): Typing "[[" opens a command popover of recent+all files filtered by query with arrow/Enter selection; choosing an existing path inserts a wikiLink node, and a "Create" option makes a new .md and links it.

User Story: As a user, I want an @ menu, so that I can summon the AI assistant.
Expected Behavior (from code): Typing "@" at a word boundary opens a popover offering "@solomon" (Research, schedule, or run tasks); selecting it inserts the @solomon trigger.

User Story: As a user, I want to give the AI a one-off instruction in the note, so that it edits/answers inline.
Expected Behavior (from code): Typing @solomon opens RowboatMentionPopover; a one-time instruction inserts a processing taskBlock, calls inline-task:process, then replaces the block with the response.

Feature: Inline AI task converts note to live (@solomon recurring)
User Story: As a user, I want a recurring instruction, so that the note self-updates on a schedule.
Expected Behavior (from code): When inline-task:process returns a schedule, the taskBlock stores schedule/label/targetId, sets live_note:true frontmatter, and writes task-target comment tags to disk.

User Story: As a writer, I want Tab to indent lists, so that I can nest items without losing focus.
Expected Behavior (from code): TabIndentExtension sinks/lifts task or list items on Tab/Shift-Tab and otherwise inserts two spaces, always consuming the key so focus stays in the editor.

User Story: As a reader, I want #heading links and [[Note#Heading]] to scroll, so that I can jump within long notes.
Expected Behavior (from code): Clicking a wikiLink with a heading fragment (or an "#" anchor link) scrolls to the matching heading by exact text or slug match and moves the caret.

User Story: As a reader, I want links to open correctly, so that http links go to the browser and file links open locally.
Expected Behavior (from code): Click handling opens http/mailto/tel via window.open and resolves relative/workspace paths to invoke shell:openPath.

User Story: As a writer, I want GFM tables, so that I can present tabular data.
Expected Behavior (from code): TableKit (non-resizable) provides table editing and renderTableToMarkdown serializes tables back to pipe-table markdown.

User Story: As a writer, I want mermaid blocks to render as diagrams, so that I can embed flowcharts.
Expected Behavior (from code): MermaidRenderer lazy-loads mermaid, initializes with the resolved light/dark theme and securityLevel strict, renders SVG, and shows an "Invalid mermaid syntax" fallback with the raw source on error.

User Story: As a user, I want special fenced blocks (task, prompt, chart, table, calendar, email, transcript, embed, iframe, image) to render as interactive cards, so that structured content stays rich.
Expected Behavior (from code): Dedicated node extensions parse/serialize each fenced block type round-trip to its fence in markdown.

User Story: As a writer, I want my blank lines kept, so that note formatting round-trips through the editor.
Expected Behavior (from code): Markdown is preprocessed to convert 3+ newlines into zero-width-space empty paragraphs and re-serialized with a custom join, then post-processed to strip the markers on save.

User Story: As a user, I want undo/redo, so that I can revert edits.
Expected Behavior (from code): The editor exposes undo/redo handlers (editor.chain().focus().undo()/redo()) to the app via onHistoryHandlersChange; baseline content loads are excluded from history (addToHistory:false).

User Story: As a user creating a new note, I want the title heading auto-focused and protected, so that typing renames the note cleanly.
